rationale: The complete journal text on pp. 1524–1525 reports three cases of ocular inflammation after contact with pet tarantula hairs. It describes topical treatment and persistent panuveitis in two cases. Sage Publications occurs in a reference from the preceding article, which shares the printed page. The tarantula report includes no fresh sage or Parkinson pain comparison.

Publisher pages 3877–3887 present. The crystal structure experiment examines yeast ubiquitin hydrolase and substrate specificity. The Figure 1 caption uses orange for drawn residue highlights. Clinical Parkinson references discuss ubiquitin pathway genetics. The paper includes no citrus intervention or falls measurement.

The telehealth study measured visit patterns and patient satisfaction. The introduction describes a remote motor rating modification that omits rigidity and postural instability. No ground sage or Parkinson rigidity response to an ingredient is tested.

The original mortality cohort enrolled 191 older COVID-19 inpatients with neurological or psychiatric conditions. Six percent had parkinsonism. Methods and risk tables concern clinical factors and in-hospital mortality. The study has no food assignment or date-fruit pain measurement.

People with Parkinson disease were assessed across dopaminergic medication states. A subgroup had larger on–off changes in clinician-rated anxiety, depression and motor scores. The phrase to date describes prior literature. No dried date preparation or attributable pain comparison appears in the cohort.

This uncontrolled retrospective cannabinoid prescribing study screened 826 eligible chronic pain patients. It reported at least 30% pain improvement for 17% and 10% of the eligible cohort at the two follow-ups using the authors' intention-to-treat estimates. Attrition was substantial. It did not test dried dates or a dried-date comparison in Parkinson disease.

The transgenic mouse study measures neuromuscular junction changes and muscle atrophy in an alpha-synuclein model. Clinical muscle pain is discussed as background. No dried-date exposure or clinical pain comparison was tested.

MAESTRO studied mirabegron plus behavioral training versus placebo plus training for overactive bladder in Parkinson disease. The primary bladder symptom endpoint was unmet. Date and dated are diary and consent fields. No dried dates were assigned and no date-specific pain contrast was measured.

This pancreatic panniculitis case describes arthralgia and tender skin nodules in a young adult with a sarcoma. Up to date describes immunization history. No dried dates or Parkinson pain comparison appears in the report.

The home-visit and peer-mentoring intervention tracked caregiver strain against historical controls. Mentors recorded the calendar date of calls. The study gives no dried-date intervention or participant pain estimate attributable to food.

The two cases describe different timing of olfactory hallucinations in migraine. To date describes the state of headache classification. Neither clinical case examines dried date fruit consumption or Parkinson pain.

The retrospective telerehabilitation comparison included 57 online-training and 29 nonexercising participants with Parkinson disease. It examined quality of life, walking, posture and freezing. Date is a registry field. Neither arm tests dried dates or a dated fruit pain endpoint.

The randomized lumbar stenosis protocol assigns exercise plus education or education alone. Walking capacity is primary and back and leg pain are secondary planned outcomes. There are no reported results in the protocol and no dried-date intervention.

The original p. 593 describes orofacial dyskinesia and bilateral ballistic movements after ibuprofen prescribed for osteoarthritic pain in a patient with prior neuroleptic-related dyskinesia. The ballistic movements diminished after ibuprofen withdrawal. The case gives no dried-date exposure or Parkinson pain comparison.

The treadmill intervention and resting-state brain-network measurements concern exercise and motor function. Figure abbreviations identify images and plots. Rest tremor is discussed as a clinical feature, with no raw fig exposure or fig-specific rest-tremor comparison.

The early-onset Parkinson series assessed 46 people around subthalamic stimulation. The within-genotype apathy changes were inconclusive and the study reports an across-subgroup difference in change. To date in one clinical narrative refers to follow-up. The apathy measures are stimulation context, with no dried-date intervention.

In a retrospective Parkinson imaging study, the matched impulsive-compulsive behavior groups had mean Apathy Scale scores 16.2 versus 15.9, p=.76. The exposure classification is behavioral, with matching on dopamine agonist dose among other factors. Nothing in the comparison tests dried-date consumption.
